Appendix B • Proofs & Comments

B.13 Reparametrization invariance of the length (§7.2)

Let \((\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}, \mathcal{A}, g)\) be a Riemannian metric manifold, \(\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to \mathcal{M}\) a smooth curve with speed \(s_\gamma\), and \(a < b\). Recall that \(L_{[a,b]}[\gamma] \coloneqq \int_a^b s_\gamma(\lambda) \, d\lambda\), where the integral exists because \(s_\gamma\), the square root of a continuous non-negative function, is continuous on \([a,b]\).

Reparametrizations. A reparametrization is a diffeomorphism \(\textrm{\runic ᚱ} : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\), i.e. a smooth bijection with smooth inverse. Equivalently, \(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}\) is a smooth bijection with \(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}'(\tilde{\lambda}) \neq 0\) for all \(\tilde{\lambda} \in \mathbb{R}\):

  • If \(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}^{-1}\) is differentiable, applying the chain rule to \(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}^{-1} \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ} = \mathrm{id}_\mathbb{R}\) gives \((\textrm{\runic ᚱ}^{-1})'\big( \textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\tilde{\lambda}) \big) \cdot \textrm{\runic ᚱ}'(\tilde{\lambda}) = 1\), so \(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}'(\tilde{\lambda}) \neq 0\).

  • Conversely, if \(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}'(\tilde{\lambda}) \neq 0\) everywhere, the inverse function theorem makes \(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}^{-1}\) smooth, with derivative \((\textrm{\runic ᚱ}^{-1})'(\lambda) = 1 / \textrm{\runic ᚱ}'\big( \textrm{\runic ᚱ}^{-1}(\lambda) \big)\).

A smooth bijection alone does not suffice: \(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\tilde{\lambda}) = \tilde{\lambda}^3\) is one, but \(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}'(0) = 0\) and its inverse, \(\lambda \mapsto \lambda^{1/3}\), is not differentiable at \(0\). Since \(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}'\) is continuous and never vanishes, it has a constant sign: \(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}\) is either orientation preserving (\(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}' > 0\)) or orientation reversing (\(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}' < 0\)). In both cases \(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}^{-1}([a,b])\) is a closed interval \([\tilde{a}, \tilde{b}]\), with \(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\tilde{a}) = a\), \(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\tilde{b}) = b\) in the first case and \(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\tilde{a}) = b\), \(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\tilde{b}) = a\) in the second.

Statement. For every reparametrization \(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}\), the reparametrized curve \(\delta \coloneqq \gamma \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}\), which traces the same path as \(\gamma\), satisfies \[ L_{[\tilde{a}, \tilde{b}]}[\delta] = L_{[a,b]}[\gamma], \qquad [\tilde{a}, \tilde{b}] \coloneqq \textrm{\runic ᚱ}^{-1}\big( [a,b] \big). \]

Proof.

  • Velocities. At every \(\tilde{\lambda} \in \mathbb{R}\), both curves pass through the same point, \(\delta(\tilde{\lambda}) = \gamma\big( \textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\tilde{\lambda}) \big)\), so their velocities live in the same tangent space. For every \(f \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\), the ordinary chain rule for the composition of the real functions \(f \circ \gamma\) and \(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}\) gives \[ v_{\delta(\tilde{\lambda})}(f) = \big( (f \circ \gamma) \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ} \big)'(\tilde{\lambda}) = (f \circ \gamma)'\big( \textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\tilde{\lambda}) \big) \cdot \textrm{\runic ᚱ}'(\tilde{\lambda}) = \textrm{\runic ᚱ}'(\tilde{\lambda}) \cdot v_{\gamma, \gamma(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\tilde{\lambda}))}(f). \] Since this holds for every \(f\), the two velocities are proportional, \[ v_{\delta(\tilde{\lambda})} = \textrm{\runic ᚱ}'(\tilde{\lambda}) \, v_{\gamma, \gamma(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\tilde{\lambda}))} \in T_{\delta(\tilde{\lambda})}\mathcal{M}. \]

  • Speeds. By the bilinearity of \(g_{\delta(\tilde{\lambda})}\), \[ s_\delta(\tilde{\lambda}) = \sqrt{ g_{\delta(\tilde{\lambda})}\big( v_{\delta(\tilde{\lambda})}, v_{\delta(\tilde{\lambda})} \big) } = \sqrt{ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}'(\tilde{\lambda})^2 \; g_{\gamma(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\tilde{\lambda}))}\big( v_{\gamma, \gamma(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\tilde{\lambda}))}, v_{\gamma, \gamma(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\tilde{\lambda}))} \big) } = |\textrm{\runic ᚱ}'(\tilde{\lambda})| \; s_\gamma\big( \textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\tilde{\lambda}) \big). \]

  • Lengths. Substituting \(\lambda = \textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\tilde{\lambda})\), \(d\lambda = \textrm{\runic ᚱ}'(\tilde{\lambda}) \, d\tilde{\lambda}\), in the orientation preserving case, \(|\textrm{\runic ᚱ}'| = \textrm{\runic ᚱ}'\), \[ L_{[\tilde{a}, \tilde{b}]}[\delta] = \int_{\tilde{a}}^{\tilde{b}} s_\gamma\big( \textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\tilde{\lambda}) \big) \, \textrm{\runic ᚱ}'(\tilde{\lambda}) \, d\tilde{\lambda} = \int_{\textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\tilde{a})}^{\textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\tilde{b})} s_\gamma(\lambda) \, d\lambda = \int_a^b s_\gamma(\lambda) \, d\lambda = L_{[a,b]}[\gamma]. \] In the orientation reversing case, \(|\textrm{\runic ᚱ}'| = -\textrm{\runic ᚱ}'\), and the extra sign compensates the exchange of the integration limits, \[ L_{[\tilde{a}, \tilde{b}]}[\delta] = -\int_{\tilde{a}}^{\tilde{b}} s_\gamma\big( \textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\tilde{\lambda}) \big) \, \textrm{\runic ᚱ}'(\tilde{\lambda}) \, d\tilde{\lambda} = -\int_{b}^{a} s_\gamma(\lambda) \, d\lambda = \int_a^b s_\gamma(\lambda) \, d\lambda = L_{[a,b]}[\gamma]. \qquad \square \]

Remarks.

  • The speed itself is not invariant: \(s_\delta = |\textrm{\runic ᚱ}'| \, (s_\gamma \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}) \neq s_\gamma \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}\) in general. Only its integral is, because the factor \(|\textrm{\runic ᚱ}'|\) is exactly the Jacobian of the change of integration variable. This is why the speed is a property of the parametrized curve, while the length is a property of the path it traces.

  • The square root in the definition of \(s_\gamma\) is what produces \(|\textrm{\runic ᚱ}'|\) rather than \(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}'\), making the length also independent of the direction in which the path is traversed.
